content: 1. Colistin Regimen for Pan-Resistant Isolates: Colistin at a dose of 5 mg/kg/day administered intravenously every 12 hours, with or without the addition of Imipenem, is the preferred treatment regimen for pan-resistant isolates. 2. Ampicillin/Sulbactam for Pan-Resistant Isolates: Ampicillin/Sulbactam is another preferred regimen for treating pan-resistant isolates. 3. Alternative Regimens for Various Infections: Ceftriaxone: Administer 1–2 g intravenously once daily. Cefotaxime: Administer 2–3 g intravenously every 6–8 hours. Ciprofloxacin: Administer 400 mg intravenously every 8–12 hours or 750 mg orally twice daily. TMP-SMX (Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole): Administer 15–20 mg (TMP component) per kg per day intravenously every 6–8 hours or 2 double-strength tablets orally twice daily. 4. Aeromonas hydrophila Infections: Diarrhea: If not self-limiting or severe, the preferred regimen is Ciprofloxacin 500 mg orally twice daily. An alternative is TMP-SMX (1 double-strength tablet orally twice daily). Note that high resistance to sulfa agents has been reported in Taiwan and Spain. Severe Infection or Sepsis: Preferred regimens include Ciprofloxacin 400 mg intravenously every 8 hours or Levofloxacin 750 mg intravenously every 24 hours. For water-based injuries, empiric coverage for Vibrio species with Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily is recommended. Fluoroquinolones may also provide coverage. For Gram-positive toxin inhibition, Vancomycin 15 mg/kg intravenously every 12 hours, with or without Clindamycin or Linezolid, can be used. Alternatives to fluoroquinolones for Aeromonas coverage include carbapenems (Ertapenem, Doripenem, Imipenem, or Meropenem), Ceftriaxone, Cefepime, and Aztreonam. 5. Bordetella pertussis Treatment: Adults: Azithromycin: 500 mg orally as a single dose on day 1, followed by 250 mg orally daily for days 2–5. Erythromycin: 2 g/day orally in four divided doses for 14 days. Clarithromycin: 1 g orally twice daily for 7 days. Infants ≥6 months and Children: Azithromycin: 10 mg/kg as a single dose on day 1, followed by 5 mg/kg daily (maximum 500 mg) for 2–5 days. Erythromycin: 40–50 mg/kg orally in four divided doses (maximum 2 g daily) for 14 days. Clarithromycin: 15 mg/kg orally in two divided doses (maximum 1 g daily) for 7 days. TMP-SMX: 8 mg/kg/day (TMP component) and 40 mg/kg/day (SMX component) in two divided doses for 14 days. Post-Exposure Prophylaxis: Antibiotic regimens are similar to those used for treatment. Prophylaxis is recommended for asymptomatic contacts within 21 days of cough onset in the index patient to prevent symptomatic infection. Close contacts include those with direct exposure to respiratory, oral, or nasal secretions of a symptomatic patient. High-risk contacts include infants <1 year, individuals with immunodeficiency, or those with chronic lung disease. 6. Burkholderia cepacia Complex: Preferred regimens include: Ceftazidime 2 g intravenously every 8 hours. Imipenem 1 g intravenously every 6 hours. Meropenem 1–2 g intravenously every 8 hours. Minocycline 100 mg intravenously or orally twice daily. 7. Burkholderia pseudomallei Eradication Therapy: TMP-SMX at a dose of 6/30 mg/kg (up to 320/1600 mg/kg) every 12 hours for a minimum of 3 months. 8. Campylobacter fetus Serious Infections: Preferred regimens include: Gentamicin 5 mg/kg intravenously every 24 hours. Imipenem 1 g intravenously every 6 hours. Ceftriaxone 2 g intravenously every 12 hours. 9. Capnocytophaga canimorsus Severe Cellulitis/Sepsis or Endocarditis: Preferred regimens: Ampicillin/Sulbactam 3 g intravenously every 6 hours. Penicillin G 2–4 million units intravenously every 24 hours for non-beta-lactamase-producing strains. Alternative regimens include Ceftriaxone, Meropenem, or Clindamycin combined with other agents for complicated infections. 10. Helicobacter pylori Triple Therapy: Preferred regimen: A proton pump inhibitor (PPI) at standard doses twice daily, Amoxicillin 1 g twice daily, and Metronidazole 500 mg twice daily. Alternatives for Amoxicillin allergy: PPI with Clarithromycin and Metronidazole, or PPI with Tetracycline and Metronidazole. 11. Legionella pneumophila Pneumonia: Preferred regimens: Levofloxacin 750 mg orally or intravenously daily for 7–10 days. Moxifloxacin 400 mg orally or intravenously daily for 7–10 days. Azithromycin 500 mg orally or intravenously daily for 7–10 days. Rifampin 300 mg orally or intravenously twice daily in combination with other agents. Alternative regimens include Erythromycin or Ciprofloxacin. 12. Salmonella Gastroenteritis: Antimicrobial therapy is generally not recommended for uncomplicated diarrheal illness. For carrier state: Ciprofloxacin 500 mg orally twice daily for 4–6 weeks. TMP-SMX 1 double-strength tablet orally twice daily for 6 weeks. Amoxicillin 500 mg orally for 6 weeks. This is a detailed, professional-level explanation of the regimens provided.
